column1: # ARC 3 / R13 -- THE ADJUDICATED CEILINGS OF THE EXTERNAL-TRUTH FLOW
# One row per (leg, isa).  A leg's HEADLINE is the count of rows where the
# tracer drops information a reference states, or where the difference is not
# understood.  The CEILING is the value a maintainer has adjudicated, row by
# row, in the verdict named in ADJUDICATION.  The gate FAILS when a headline
# EXCEEDS its ceiling, when a report is missing, when a headline cannot be
# parsed, or when the leg's scored population is below FLOOR.
# A ceiling is never a target.  RETIRED_BY names the work item whose landing
# must lower it; a ceiling with no RETIRED_BY is one this project accepts as
# a property of the reference, not of the trace.

RE-POINTED AT THE OFFLINE REFEREE.  THE x86_64 STATIC-DECODE LEG drove build/contrib/plugins/isaxcheck, a binary that linked Capstone into the build and was deleted with it, so this row had NO PRODUCER at the tip and read REPORT MISSING -- a red about the apparatus and not about the trace.  Per the standing external-comparison ruling the reference now runs OFFLINE over recorded encodings, and the row is re-pointed at the successor rather than retired: cst_referee.py decodes the recorded encodings offline and gapreport.py joins its opcode word against QEMU's, one bucket per encoding, with every disagreement class arbitrated in gapreport_rulings.tsv. The headline is UNRULED encodings (the difference nobody has read) PLUS COVERAGE-PATH encodings (read, and the reference won: the wire owes a change).  Arbitrated-to-QEMU encodings are outside it, exactly as TRACER-SUPERSET was. NO MARGIN: a headline of 4 is a finding to open.  FLOOR 95000 against 105,762 encodings joined with the reference at this tip.  THE STALE FIXTURE IS GONE WITH THE ROW: the selftest default carried 47 against a ceiling of 11 because the banked root predates exec179's re-derivation; the successor report is regenerated at the tip as part of this re-point and the fixture moves with it per #305. exec246 RE-DERIVATION (2026-09-18) at 855a9c12dc, both aarch64 legs re-run at one tip.  HEADLINE 51 -> 49 = 36 TRACER-SUBSET + 13 UNACCOUNTED over 1,003 facts / 210 distinct encodings, no axis INERT.  CEILING HELD AT 22 AND THE ROW IS STILL RED.  WHAT MOVED IS EXACTLY THREE ROWS, THEY ARE THE 244-C DE-INTERLEAVING LOADS, AND rows.tsv NAMES EACH.  (1) 0x4000ec `ld2 {v15.16b,v16.16b},[x21]' was ref={REG_VEC15,REG_VEC16} trc={} NO-LABEL UNACCOUNTED and now AGREES -- the row is gone from the file.  (2) 0x4000f4 `ld4 {v20.16b..v23.16b}' was ref={REG_VEC20,REG_VEC21,REG_VEC22,REG_VEC23} trc={} and now AGREES.  (3) 0x4000f0 `ld3 {v17.16b,v18.16b,v19.16b}' was ref={REG_VEC17,REG_VEC18,REG_VEC19,REG_VEC20} trc={} and now publishes trc={REG_VEC17,REG_VEC18,REG_VEC19} -- the three registers LD3 actually writes -- and the row carries REF-NEON-PAIRWISE-DEST.  THAT RULE PREDATES THIS WAVE and its own text already names the form: `gem5 names vector destinations in pairs; the odd-count LD1/LD1R/LD3 forms gain one register that is not written'.  It could not fire before because its predicate is len(ra) == len(ta) + (len(ta) & 1) over vector names, which an empty tracer set can never satisfy.  SO TRACER-SUBSET 35 -> 36 IS AN UNACCOUNTED ROW ACQUIRING A PRE-EXISTING LABEL, NOT A NEW DISAGREEMENT, and the parity predicate is its own control: it accepted the odd-count LD3 and had nothing to say about the even-count LD2 and LD4, which is what the mechanism predicts.  Corroborated off the axis table: trc_writes 244 -> 253, and 9 = 2+3+4 is exactly the destination count of ld2, ld3 and ld4; reg-dst-set agreement 224 -> 226 over 255.  THE WAVE'S STATED PREMISE IS CORRECTED TWICE, by measurement.  First, the cause was not `their OWN field count overflows the caps' alone: the stores fail on MEMOPS by itself (incompleteness word 0x4) and the loads on FIELDS|MEMOPS (0x6), so the memop overflow is common to both and is the whole of the store side.  Second, there was no x86 FXSAVE mechanism to copy -- 79b87bcf4b priced two routes and explicitly built neither.  THE REPAIR (f731940227) IS NOT A CAP BUMP: a decode-site statement (insn_dataflow_note_split_access, called only where a->selem != 1) tells the reader that the lowering's per-element accesses are one architectural access, and df_add_field merges an adjacent WRITE row that lies in the same declared container with identical provenance.  The cap bump was priced and rejected -- memops 16 -> 64 alone is about 1.7 MiB per thread of static scratch.  WHAT IS LEFT, 49, IS NAMED.  The 36 TRACER-SUBSET all carry a rule (5 reference-defect, 28 vocabulary-difference, 3 emulation-artefact).  The 13 UNACCOUNTED are 12 memop rows -- 4 each on memop-count, memop-addr and memop-width -- at p_cache 0x4000bc/c0/c4 (`dc cvau, x21', `dc civac, x21', `dc cvac, x21'), where gem5 issues one 64-byte access and the wire publishes NO memop at all, plus 1 ORTHOGONAL reg-dst-set row.  THE 12 ARE A REAL UNREPAIRED LOSS and their fix path is written out in full on this wave's gem5wp/aarch64 row, residue R2.  Prior adjudication, unchanged for everything that did not move: R13_VERDICT.md 4.1

exec245 RE-MEASUREMENT (2026-09-18, four arms on ONE build: BASE, after the FR=0 preserve-read fix, after the condition-code write statement, and at the final tree).  HEADLINE 3 -> 1, CEILING HELD AT 1, AND THE CEILING'S OLD BASIS IS SPENT SO RETIRED_BY GOES TO `-'.  The exec244 text's headline of 10 was read before the accumulator landing: at this base 02d2e16c44 the six mult/multu/div/divu/madd/msub rows and their sibling are GONE, because REG_ACCHI0 now has an id of its own, so #282 -- the work item this row named as its retiring condition -- has already done what it could here.  WHAT THIS WAVE MOVED, measured in place: the 2 FPSR-GRANULARITY rows on `c.eq.s' at 0x400148 and `c.lt.s' at 0x40014c, where the reference named REG_FCSR as a destination and the wire named nothing.  It was not a granularity difference at all: the architectural destination of c.cond.fmt is FCC[cc], a field of FCR31, and every cmp helper writes it with SET_FP_COND()/CLEAR_FP_COND() on env->active_fpu.fcr31 from INSIDE the helper, so fpu_fcr31 is never an op's output and the destination reached the wire as nothing.  Stated once for the whole family, in the FOP_CONDS macro after the two operand loads, which is the one place every form passes through; the A/B is on one build and the rows moved exactly with it (BASE 3, preserve-read arm 3, statement arm 1).  THE ONE SURVIVOR, named: `cfc1 r9, f31' at p_fp 0x40013c, reg-dst-value, ref REG_GPR9=0 against trc REG_GPR9=4108.  FIR is a machine-IDENTITY register -- implementation, revision and feature bits -- and the two models describe different machines, so neither value is wrong and there is no datum being dropped.  No work item can retire it: RETIRED_BY is `-' and this is accepted as a property of the reference pair.  NO MARGIN: a headline of 2 is a finding.  43 disagreeing rows total, 42 TRACER-SUPERSET all named, 0 UNACCOUNTED, no axis INERT over 432 facts / 114 subjects.  Prior adjudication superseded in its headline and its RETIRED_BY: the exec244 text (23 -> 10, ceiling 1, #282), whose accumulator half landed.

exec246 RE-DERIVATION (2026-09-18) at 855a9c12dc, both aarch64 legs re-run at one tip.  HEADLINE 114 -> 96 over 40,798 facts / 125 encodings, no axis INERT; TRACER-SUPERSET 195 and UNACCOUNTED 0 both unchanged.  CEILING HELD AT 0 AND THE ROW IS STILL RED.  TWO CAUSES MOVED, EIGHTEEN ROWS.  (a) reg-src-set 12 WP-DEFECT -> 0, FIXED AT SOURCE in bfd6ad19e6.  `dc cvau, x21' and `dc civac, x21' are ARM_CP_NOP (target/arm/helper.c, `Cache ops: all NOPs since we don't emulate caches') and handle_sys() returned before anything read Xt, so the wire published src=[] for an instruction whose operand is a register.  THE CONTROL WAS BUILT IN AND NOT CONSTRUCTED FOR THE OCCASION: `ic ivau, x21' sits between the two, is NOT a NOP (it carries ic_ivau_write, so the generic path reads Xt) and published src=[REG_GPR21] on the same trace where its two neighbours published nothing.  Three adjacent cache operations, one difference between them, and it was that return.  The statement is read-direction only: on the isread direction the architecture writes Xt and QEMU does not, so publishing a write there would name a destination the emulation never produced.  (b) fpsr-dst-set 36 WP-DEFECT -> 30 WP-DEFECT + 6 GEM5-LIMIT, by the rule 855a9c12dc landed.  The 6 are ref=[MISC:ic_ivau_xt] against trc=[]; MISCREG_IC_IVAU_Xt (gem5 src/arch/arm/regs/misc.hh) is the slot gem5's decoder parks the operand in so its own execute method can read it back, the architecture gives IC IVAU no destination register, and there is therefore no architectural write for the tracer to have dropped.  The rule ASKS THE MAPPER (gem5_ref.ref_can_name) rather than keying on the `MISC:' spelling, and is held to the SUBSET direction.  WHAT IS LEFT, 96, IS TWO RESIDUES AND BOTH ARE REAL UNREPAIRED LOSS, STATED AS SUCH.  R1 -- 60 rows: 30 fpsr-dst-set ref=[REG_FCSR] and 30 sys-src-set ref=[REG_FCSR,REG_FLAGS,REG_SYSFPEN], on p_wpmem's fadd/fmul/fcvt.  QEMU DOES model the FPSR read and write; it lives in softfloat's float_status, reached through fpstatus_ptr().  The wire drops it because target/arm installs NO helper-usage table -- target/i386/tcg/insn-df-usage.c is the only one in the tree -- and insn_dataflow_declare_helper_usage() refuses a partial one, so closing this is a table for target/arm's whole helper surface: a wave of its own, not a tail item.  RULING IT REFERENCE-SIDE WOULD BE A FALSE JUSTIFICATION AND IS REFUSED -- gem5 is right, these instructions read and write the FP status word.  R2 -- 36 rows, 12 each on memop-count, memop-addr and memop-width, at p_wpcache 0x4000dc/e0/e4 (`dc cvau, x21', `ic ivau, x21', `dc civac, x21').  The reference issues 64 single-byte stores over S:0x410540..0x41057f; the wire publishes 0L/0S.  THE BRIEF'S PREMISE IS CORRECTED ON THREE COUNTS, each read off the report: it is 36 rows and not 48, the instructions are dc cvau / ic ivau / dc civac and not dc zva, and the shape is an ABSENT access rather than a different split -- SAME-BYTES-DIFFERENT-SPLIT cannot apply because the tracer publishes no bytes at all.  NO RULE IS WRITTEN FOR THEM, DELIBERATELY: this leg reaches its cache-maintenance rules through _addr_only(t), which requires the trace to publish at least one memop with every size 0, and then separates maintenance from prefetch by whether the trace's own write list carries REG_SYSCACHE.  Both discriminators are the TRACE's facts by design (`WHICH mechanism is read off the trace's own write list, never off a mnemonic'), this trace supplies neither, so there is nothing a rule may key on, and keying on the pc or the mnemonic is the shape the leg forbids.  THE FIX IS AT SOURCE AND IS NOW EXACTLY NAMED: the ARM_CP_NOP arm of handle_sys() must mint the size-0 synthetic access with insn_dataflow_note_synthetic_ea, as the DC ZVA arm a few lines below it already does, and publish REG_SYSCACHE as the maintenance destination.  NOT DONE IN THIS WAVE, and the blocker is the one that DC ZVA arm's own comment states: separating the by-VA forms from the by-set/way and `all' forms needs a QEMU-side source, and guessing from the crm field would be invention.  ONE CANDIDATE SOURCE WAS FOUND AND IS RECORDED AS UNVERIFIED, not as a basis: in helper.c the by-VA maintenance cpregs (DC_CVAC, DC_CVAU, DC_CIVAC, IC_IVAU) carry .access = PL0_W with a per-operation .fgt bit while the set/way and `all' forms (DC_ISW, DC_CSW, DC_CISW, IC_IALLU) are PL1_W -- which matches the architecture, since only the by-VA forms are available at EL0 under SCTLR_EL1.UCI.  The enumeration that would turn that into a checkable basis was not completed here, so it is written down as a lead and nothing was landed on it.  Prior adjudication, unchanged: R13_VERDICT.md 5.1 -- 15/15 axis mutations FIRED, 8/8 cache-maintenance rules REFUSED

exec244 RE-DERIVATION (2026-09-18, all 20 rows measured fresh at one tip). HEADLINE 257 -> 105 = 20 WP-DEFECT + 85 UNACCOUNTED over 5,553 facts / 109 encodings, 42 excursions, no axis INERT.  CEILING HELD AT 0.  THE TWO CLASSES THE x87 LANDING MINTED ARE RULED HERE ON WRITTEN MERITS, AND BOTH ARE TRACER-RIGHT.  (A) 60 UNACCOUNTED reg-dst-set rows, twelve x87 PCs (0x40101d..0x401045) x 5 excursions, only_trc={REG_SYS}.  regmap/x86_64.tsv maps fpip/fpcs/fpdp/fpds to REG_SYS with its own written reason -- "x87 exception pointer: machine state saved for a handler, not a value the program computes with" -- and every non-control x87 instruction updates the last-instruction and last-data pointers, so the wire is stating a real destination.  The reference CANNOT speak: this leg's own report prints "unmappable-id:REG_SYS 42", i.e. gem5's x86 vocabulary has no index that produces REG_SYS.  Reference gap with a checkable basis in the mapper, the same shape as the REG_PC class, and the rule is derivable and NOT YET WRITTEN.  (B) 15 UNACCOUNTED reg-src-set rows at 0x401025/27/2d x 5, only_trc={REG_FCSR} against ref {REG_FPR0,REG_FPR1}.  Under the composed-register contract settled at 050283a3f1 a folded FIELD publishes its CONTAINER, so reading the rounding-control field of the x87 control word IS a read of REG_FCSR; ledger #277c asks this exact question and answers SOURCE.  Tracer right; the rule is written and not ported to this leg.  (C) THE BRIEF'S ARITHMETIC IS INCOMPLETE AND THE REMAINDER IS NOT SLACK.  60 + 15 = 75, and the headline is 105.  Ten rows at 0x401041 and 0x401043 run the OTHER way: ref={REG_FCSR,REG_FPR0} against trc={REG_FPR0,REG_SYS} -- REG_FCSR is in the reference and NOT on the wire, so two x87 PCs do not publish their status-word write.  That is a LOSS, filed as FINDING 244-D.  (D) 20 WP-DEFECT reg-src-set: 15 on p_wprmw at 0x40104d/0x401062/0x401095 with only_ref={REG_FLAGS}, and 5 on p_wpsse 0x40102b with ref={REG_VEC2} against trc={} -- the x86 sibling of 244-C, a vector source not published at all.  (E) 10 UNACCOUNTED reg-src-set on p_wpchain 0x40102a and p_wpflag 0x401047, only_ref={REG_FLAGS}.  So 75 rows are tracer-right and want rules, and 35 are real losses with two findings against them.  Prior adjudication, unchanged: exec33/flagsleak/EVIDENCE.md -- the leg EXISTS and RUNS; R13_VERDICT.md 5/8.1's "x86_64 has no wrong-path execution reference" is FALSE as written

exec245 RE-MEASUREMENT (2026-09-18, three arms on ONE build: BASE, after the FR=0 preserve-read fix, after the store-conditional source statement).  HEADLINE 32 -> 4, CEILING 10 -> 4, and the row's OLD RETIRED_BY list is spent: #269 and #221 named the FR=0 FP-pair class, and THAT CLASS IS NOT WHAT THE HEADLINE WAS.  MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: at BASE the 26 UNACCOUNTED rows on p_wpfp were all strict TRACER-SUPERSET on 13 pcs, every one trc={REG_FPRn, REG_GPR16} against ref={REG_GPR16} -- the DESTINATION of an FP store named as a SOURCE of it.  CAUSE: TCG cannot write part of a global, so gen_store_fpr32/32h/64 lower a narrow FP write as tcg_gen_deposit_i64(fpu_f64[r], fpu_f64[r], ...), and the merge's read of the destination reached the op walk as an ordinary operand read.
